text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English explorer Sir WILLIAM PARRY, who searched for the Northwest Passage, was born in 1790.
The first Australian-born novelist JOHN LANG was born in 1816. His works include "The Forger's Wife" and "Botany Bay". Ironically he spent much of his life in India and England.
Australian pastoralist WILLIAM MORTON, who invented the swing-gate and the sheep-dip, was born in 1820.
West Australian pioneer EMMA WITHNELL, who was known as "Mother of the North West", was born in 1842. One of her 11 children, JOHN, discovered gold at Pilbara.

The poor French street singer EDITH PIAF, who was known as "The Little Sparrow", was born in 1915. Her father reportedly made her sing in the streets of Paris to earn money. She was discovered by a night club owner and had a million seller with her song "La Vie En Rose" in 1950.
British actor GORDON JACKSON, who appeared in many films including "Tunes of Glory", was born in 1923. He was best known for his role of the butler in the television series "Upstairs, Downstairs".

US singer, drummer and songwriter with 'Earth, Wind and Fire' MAURICE WHITE was born in 1941. He began working in the sixties and played with BILLY STEWART, CHUCK BERRY and ETTA JAMES. His hits included "Got To Get You Into My Life"(1978) and "After The Love Has Gone"(1979).
US guitarist, violinist and singer with the 'Nitty Gritty Dirt Band' JOHN McEUEN was born in 1945.

British singer and songwriter LIMAHL (CHRISTOPHER HAMILL) was born in 1958. His career started with the band 'Kajagoogoo'. The band's hits included "Too Shy" (1983) and "Oooh To Be Ah" (1983). His solo career hits were "Only For Love" (1983) and "Never Ending Story" (1984).
** EVENTS **
960 : Reconstruction of the Japanese Imperial Palace in
Kyoto started after it was damaged by fire.
1848 : English novelist EMILY BRONTE died of consumption
at the age of 30. Her death came three months after she caught a cold at her brother BRANWELL's funeral. Her classic novel was "Wuthering Heights".
1905 : The first-ever motorised ambulance service for
road accident victims was set up in London.
1927 : In China, 600 communists were executed by the
Nationalists.
1932 : The British Broadcasting Corporation started its

Empire shortwave broadcasting service via its new Daventry transmitter. News from England could reach every corner of the British Empire. The new service was the brainchild of JOHN REITH, who also developed radio broadcasting throughout the U.K.
1958 : US President DWIGHT EISENHOWER wished the world a
very special Merry Christmas - the first relayed around the world via satellite.
1969 : In a busy day on the stock exchange Poseidon

shares jumped to a high of 130 dollars, before settling back to 126 dollars. The share price increase followed the company's announcement in Adelaide that it intended to start a nickel mine in Western Australia. A few years earlier Poseidon shares were selling for six cents each. They later peaked at about 280 dollars in early 1970.
1982 : The Kangaroos hailed as the "best rugby side in
the world" became the first Australian rugby league touring team to win all 22 matches in Britain and France, including five tests.
1984 : Britain and China signed an historic agreement

sealing the fate of Hong Kong after the 99-year lease of the New Territories expires in 1997. Despite protests Britain agreed to return all of its holdings in return for assurances that Hong Kong's lifestyle would be preserved for at least 50 years. Hong Kong will become a special administrative region within China, with its own laws, currency, budget and taxation. It will retain the right to negotiate separate international trade agreements. It's not known if China will honour these commitments and the Hong Kong community felt betrayed by Britain.
1991 : President of the USSR MIKHAIL GORBACHEV resigned.
The Soviet Union had ceased to exist a week earlier. Although he survived a coup the previous year he was virtually forced to resign by his rival BORIS YELSTIN.
1991 : The Australian Labor Party caucus deposed prime
minister BOB HAWKE after eight years in office and replaced him with treasurer PAUL KEATING. HAWKE was bitter about the leadership challenge and his subsequent defeat.
